Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Hare Krishna Tripathi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the material available on record.
This application for anticipatory bail has been filed by applicant - Jagat Narayan in connection with Case Crime No.04 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 323, 306 I.P.C., P.S.- Bah, District- Agra.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has no concern with the present matter.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
Investigation is going on in the matter.
Applicant's case is squarely covered under Section 438 Cr.P.C. If the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty and will cooperate with the investigation.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest by the police any time.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
It appears from the perusal of the F.I.R. that general allegations have been made against the accused persons.
A specific plea of separate living has been taken by the accused-applicant.
It also appears from the perusal of the record that some independent witnesses have supported the aforesaid plea taken by the accused-applicant.

It also appears from the perusal of the record that earlier the Jagat Narayan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123824871/
1 accused-applicant was granted anticipatory bail till filing of the police report under Section 173(2)
Cr.P.C. passed in CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. -
10841 of 2021 (Jagat Narayan Vs. State of U.P. and Another) by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 15.02.2022.

sentences.text: It further reveals from the perusal of the record that the aforesaid liberty granted by the Court was never misused by the present accused-applicant.
In the post-mortem report, cause of death was found as "Asphyxia" due to anti-mortem hanging and no other injury on other parts of the body have been found.
It also appears that after filing of the charge-sheet in the matter, now no custodial interrogation of the accused-applicant is appears to be required.

It further reveals from the record that no specific occasion or date has been mentioned in respect of the alleged harassment/cruelty caused to the deceased who was daughter-in-law(Bahu) of the present accused-applicant in the F.I.R. or even in the statement of the witnesses.

In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, it has been held that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, llikelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

Considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, in my view, it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. in the matter.
The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

In the event of arrest of the applicant in the aforesaid case crime, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions :-
1.
The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.

2. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
3. The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
